newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela bolivar soars, ends off peaks at 472/dlr.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela bolivar soars, ends off peaks at 472/dlr.

text.p: The Venezuelan bolivar soared against the U.S. dollar as inflows of foreign funds to the Caracas bolsa tightened bolivar supplies, but came off its highs later in the session, traders said.
The unit reached an intra-day high of 469.25/470.00 per dollar -- over five bolivars firmer than Wednesday's close of 474.60/475.10 per dollar.
But it suddenly softened at the end of the session, closing at 472.00/473.25 per dollar as banks took advantage of highly-priced bolivars to buy low-priced dollars.
"It's been crazy... we never expected to see this, the market was completely inundated with dollars," said one broker. "I've never seen anything like it before."
Market explanations clashed as some traders said the rise in the bolivar stemmed from large local investments by Coca- Cola Co.

Others traders said the bolivar's midsession appreciation was due to large portfolio investments by foreign investors in the Caracas stock exchange, which rose 2.3 percent to reach a fifth consecutive high Thursday.
In a break with recent practice, the Central Bank did not intervene during the session and only monitored the market, traders said.
Venezuela currently keeps to foreign exchange bands under which government officials have said the bolivar would depreciate by 1.5 percent a month.
